newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-CAPELLO UNDER FIRE AS REAL BETRAY ATTACKING TRADITION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CAPELLO UNDER FIRE AS REAL BETRAY ATTACKING TRADITION.

text.p: Fabio Capello's Real Madrid have walked into a barrage of criticism despite holding down second place in the Spanish first division at the weekend.
Unbeaten but unimpressive, Real have been slated by the Madrid press after scoring twice from just three shots on goal in the 2-1 victory at struggling Compostela.

Few deny the quality of the multi-billion peseta Real squad, particularly strikers Davor Suker and Predrag Mijatovic, but the negative tactics of former AC Milan coach Capello go against the team's attacking traditions.

"Real once again win `a la italiana'", read a headline in the El Pais daily. "Playing badly, very badly if necessary, scorning style, the ball and even the tradition of one of the greatest clubs in the world," continued the match report.
"Real were mean in their football, but made good use of the quality of their strikers," commented a columnist in the sports daily Marca.
The result, if not the style of play, came as good news to Real after a weekend of upheaval in the transfer market.
Sampdoria announced an agreement to sell Christian Karembeu to Barcelona just a day after Real chairman Lorenzo Sanz was boasting that the French international midfielder would go to Madrid in 1998.

Sanz took the news stoically, assuring that he had reached a verbal agreemeent with Karembeu's agent. But some newspapers have speculated Sanz will try to disrupt Real's arch-rivals by putting in an offer for key Brazil striker Ronaldo.

Elsewhere, Valencia fans are fast forgetting about another Brazilian, transferred World Cup hero Romario, but their team have still not remembered how to win after becoming the latest victims of surprise outfit Valladolid.
The 4-2 win leaves Valladolid in fourth place, less than eight months after Vicente Cantatore took on the seemingly impossible task of guiding the team from the bottom of the first division.
The Chilean led an inspired fight against relegation, and has since stunned the pundits with a series of unexpected results.
